scope: Profile native runner cleanup after failed extension reload; source and existing local evidence only

A_launch_readiness.reason: Source defects below conflict with the required failure provenance and durable pre-mutation receipt. This review did not run a browser or write the database.
A_launch_readiness.known_state: The prior owned test row was recovered and original absence restored; the underlying reload failure remains unknown. No reload acceptance case is promoted.

positive_findings: A private receipt is created with exclusive creation before the first UI save and checks that group/other mode bits are zero.
Cleanup uses an owner, organization, marker, creation timestamp, and expected version compare before deletion, then checks owner-read absence; a concurrent version change fails closed.
A failed reload before returning a replacement panel now attempts to attach a live extension panel; cleanup failure reports restoration as unverified and cannot produce a passed run.

blockers.finding: When execution and cleanup both fail, cleanupError is thrown first and becomes report.failure_code. report.execution_failure_code survives as secondary evidence, but the original execution error is still masked as the primary failure. Preserve the original as primary while recording cleanup failure separately; a failed cleanup must still mark restoration unverified.

writeFile and rename do not sync file content or the containing directory before Save. The receipt can be lost across a process or host crash after the database mutation, so the claimed durable pre-mutation ownership proof is not established. Sync the new file and directory before mutation, and sync replacement receipt updates.

attachTargetSession is outside the transient-target try block. If a target disappears between Target.getTargets and attachment, the recovery helper exits immediately rather than retrying another live panel. Put attachment and verification in one retryable block.

B_quality.remaining_verification: After source repair, use a fresh private receipt path and a bounded native run to establish whether Chrome reload itself works and whether cleanup restores absence on an actual reload failure.
